instruction.text: Fill the gaps with pronouns that refer back to the words in blue.

atoms.sound: That book is not Eleanor’s. She took it from her brother.

atoms.a: Tom hasn’t seen <t-blue>Chris or Matt</t-blue> since Monday.
atoms.sound: Tom hasn’t seen Chris or Matt since Monday. He needs to speak to them.

atoms.a: <t-blue>Julia, Megan and I</t-blue> had a sleepover.
atoms.b: ((It)) was a really fun night for ((us)).
atoms.sound: Julia, Megan and I had a sleepover. It was a really fun night for us.

atoms.a: <t-blue>My mum</t-blue> came to cheer <t-blue>Oli and me</t-blue> on.
atoms.sound: My mum came to cheer Oli and me on. She really wanted us to win.

instruction.text: What do the blue pronouns in the sentence below refer to?

atoms.a: Grace met Liam last week and had a great time. <t-blue>She</t-blue> missed <t-blue>him</t-blue> a lot.
The employees had an important meeting in the morning. <t-blue>It</t-blue> is putting <t-blue>them</t-blue> under a lot of pressure.
Jake plays tennis with Ella. <t-blue>He</t-blue> likes <t-blue>her</t-blue>.

instruction.text: Write the correct pronouns to finish the story.

atoms.b: Yesterday, my brother and I spent the day together. ((We)) bought some food and ate ((it)) in the park.
My brother and I went to cinema to watch a film. I loved it, but ((he)) was a scaredy-cat and screamed the whole way through.
Amaria and Isaac were talking in the library yesterday. A lady told ((them)) to be quiet. ((She)) was very annoyed with them!
I had lots of fun with my friends yesterday! ((We)) always have a great time together.
